scope: TaskContract / Submission / GovernanceSpec / GovernedExecutionPlan / ExecutionState ownership separation
finding: Former GovernedTaskContract combined governance inputs with mutable execution lifecycle state and Runtime mutated that state directly. DurableExecution already owned persisted runtime state, creating dual state ownership.

canonical_model.GovernedExecutionPlan: immutable plan joining Submission + GovernanceSpec + routed steps + assurance
canonical_model.AEGR: evaluates GovernanceSpec and RouteDecision; does not own execution state
canonical_model.Runtime: executes an already authorized plan and records observations; does not transition authoritative task state
canonical_model.DurableExecution: sole authoritative execution-state owner and persistence adapter
canonical_model.Evidence: observes/proves execution; does not authorize it

implemented: Introduced explicit Submission contract and separated it from TaskContract intent.
Introduced GovernanceSpec and GovernedExecutionPlan canonical contracts.
Retired the former stt_love.og.task_contract implementation; namespace exposes no legacy contract.
Migrated AEGR assurance from task/state-bearing contract to GovernanceSpec.
Migrated Runtime from plan.task state transitions to plan/submission observations plus DurableExecution snapshot.
Migrated server sync/async submission paths to enqueue_submission().
Added negative tests for legacy task keyword, direct TaskContract enqueue, legacy contract surface, and plan state aliasing.
Made TaskContract, Submission and GovernanceSpec metadata/context mapping-backed to prevent shallow mutation through frozen dataclasses.
invariants: GovernanceSpec has no execution lifecycle state
Runtime does not mutate authoritative execution state
DurableExecution is the sole execution-state owner
AEGR does not receive the legacy task/state contract
No internal caller uses GovernedTaskContract, plan.task, or enqueue_contract
